chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Joining Lew Leslie's Blackbirds at the Moulin Rouge
summary: Herb Fleming and Luke Smith recommended Briggs to the Blackbirds conductor Mr. Weir because one first trumpeter was overworked; he passed a test and was hired for the season.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So then what, you were playing around Paris, now --

Yes, yes. I played after I finished, it happened that Lew Leslie's Blackbirds came to the Moulin Rouge Theatre on Place Blanche, and I had a very, very fine friend who was with -- a trombone player -- who was with the New York 15th Division, with Lt. James Reese -- yes.
Briggs

His name was Herbert Fleming.
You've heard of him.
Sure. Herb Fleming.

Well, Herb knew
that I was in Paris, and he had Luke Smith,
one of the famous Smith --
Smith Brothers.

Smith Brothers,
trumpet players.

He was the brother
of Russell Smith and Joe Smith.
Yes.

Luke was the first trumpet player
with the show. And Luke had always been
complaining and saying how hard it was for
one trumpet player, and it's true.

One trumpet player
playing the whole show?

One first trumpet
player.
Oh.
There were three
Briggs
trumpets, but one first, you see.
Right.
He had one first. You had to get off, and you had a second.
Right.
And did you ever hear of Swayzee?
Yes.
Swayzee was the get-off trumpet.
Oh, he was.
Yeh. And the other guy was Al Brown, the second trumpet player was Al Brown. With Lew Leslie's Blackbirds.

So, Fleming knowing that I was in Paris, he contacted me. He spoke to Mr. -- to Lew Leslie and told him, he said, -- Lew told him too, he said, 'This theater is much too big for me alone, as one person and trumpet player,' and he'd have to find someone, so he said, he asked Luke, 'Do you
Briggs 201
think that you'd know someone, in Paris?" And Luke said, "Yeh, sure, Arthur Briggs, he's a friend. and I know that he can make it."
So he arranged with Mr. Weir, who was the conductor of the orchestra for a rehearsal, to see whether -- you know.
So, I made the test, and apparently it was okay, and I was hired for the entire season. So I kept on at my job until my contract expired, and did this show.
